reason: Far too large and too senior for a fractional engagement, and it sells the very capability Barry sells: Defense Unicorns is a ~165-person, $65M-revenue Series B unicorn ($136M led by Bain Capital, Jan 2026, >$1B valuation, $171-186M raised total) versus Barry's stated ICP of 8-30-person Series A/B defense startups; it was founded by the Air Force software-factory leaders behind Kessel Run and Platform One who achieved the DoD's first continuous ATO, already has a co-founder CTO (Jeff McCoy) and is hiring its own CISO, so the 'accelerate the ATO / get procurement-ready' pain Barry fixes is the product Defense Unicorns ships to others rather than a gap it needs filled.
